events.title: Wood Shop Tour
events.description: Watch master craftsmen handcrafting custom solid hardwood furniture. At George's, you’ll be transported to a different world where furniture is made by hand. Skilled craftsmen take a solid piece of cherry, oak, maple or walnut and carve it into furniture that is a functional work of art for your home. Each piece created is one-of-a kind, signed and dated by the artisan. Enjoy watching handmade furniture being built, and shop in our showroom. Woodshop Tour Hours Mon-Fri, 9 a.m.-2 p.m. Showroom hours Mon-Sat 9am–5pm. Our tour begins in our showroom where we learn about the 50+ year history of Georges furniture, from hobby to business, what makes George's different from other furniture stores, and the amazing ability of our extension tables. (Tables start at 5 ft and extend to 12+ feet with ease.) then proceed to our wood working shop where the craftsmen select the wood looking at the grain, using basic saws, jointers, sanders and planers. Next, we see the furniture be stained and protected with a water-resistant finish. Finally we see our showroom with our 21-foot dining table and our bedroom furniture. After our wood shop tour, people look at furniture a whole new way. It is very informative and impactful. Monday-Friday weekly from 9-2pm year round

events.title: Amish Butter Churning at Old Windmill Farm
events.description: Experience a Lancaster County tradition firsthand at Old Windmill Farm, an authentic working Amish farm in Ronks, PA. During this hands-on experience, you’ll learn how to churn fresh cream into butter using a tradition that has been passed down through generations of the family. The cream comes from the farm’s own cows, giving you a closer look at the connection between farming, food and everyday Amish life in Lancaster County. Once the butter is finished, enjoy a taste with crackers and lemonade before taking home a half-pound of freshly churned butter per person. It’s a simple, memorable way for families, couples and curious travelers to experience Amish Country beyond the roadside views.More Things to Do at Old Windmill FarmTake an Amish Farm Tour – Milk a cow, bottle feed calves, gather eggs, meet farm animals and enjoy a hayride around the property.Try the Amish Farm Fun Combo – Add seasonal gardening activities, including planting or harvesting fresh vegetables to take home.Meet & Cuddle Farm Animals – Get up close with goats, piglets, chicks, bunnies, calves and other animals, depending on the season.Book a Seasonal Farm Experience – Fall offerings can include baking bread, churning butter and pressing fresh apple cider in the farmhouse kitchen.Shop Farm-Fresh Goods – Stop by Windmill Harvest for items like raw milk, cheese, meat and canned goods to take home. Learn More about Old Windmill Farm Make a weekend of your visit! Old Windmill Farm is located in the heart of Lancaster County’s Amish countryside, close to restaurants, lodging and other popular attractions in Ronks, Paradise and Strasburg. Where to Eat Near Old Windmill Farm Make your Amish Country visit even more memorable with a meal nearby. Hershey Farm Grand Smorgasbord – Enjoy Pennsylvania Dutch favorites, homestyle dishes, baked goods and a full smorgasbord experience. Dienner’s Country Restaurant – A local favorite for traditional Pennsylvania Dutch comfort food, homemade dishes and buffet selections. Miller’s Smorgasbord – Experience a Lancaster County tradition with a wide selection of Pennsylvania Dutch dishes, carved meats, fresh baked desserts and more. Fireside Tavern – For something a little different, head to nearby Strasburg for steaks, seafood, sandwiches and casual American fare in a cozy tavern setting. More Places to Eat in Lancaster Places to Stay Near Old Windmill Farm Turn your butter-churning experience into an overnight getaway and spend more time exploring Lancaster County’s Amish countryside. Hershey Farm Resort – Relax on a scenic Amish Country property featuring charming guest rooms, countryside views, walking paths, an outdoor pool, and on-site Smorgasbord, gift shop, bakery, and cafe. The Red Caboose Motel at Paradise Station – Spend the night in a restored railroad caboose surrounded by Lancaster County farmland for a stay that’s especially fun for families and train lovers. Fulton Steamboat Inn – A distinctive steamboat-themed hotel with an indoor pool, on-site dining and a convenient location near attractions throughout the Route 30 and Strasburg area. The Cabins at Beaver Creek – Settle into a private cabin surrounded by the peaceful Lancaster County countryside for a quieter, more relaxed Amish Country getaway. More Places to Stay in Lancaster

events.title: Chief Uncas Sunset Cruise
events.description: Watch the Sunset over the Susquehanna! 1.5 hour Sunset Cruises give small groups (up to 16 passengers) the chance to roam the historic Chief Uncas for a personalized relaxing evening experience. Bring aboard food and B.Y.O.B. alcoholic beverages to enjoy as the Chief Uncas silently cruises under the setting sun. Store your cold drinks in the vintage ice box and use the boat’s Bluetooth speakers to play your favorite music. A knowledgeable crew member is aboard as your guide to answer questions or give a tour of the river. The perfect experience for a date night or fun time with friends! Sunset Cruises depart from the Zimmerman Center dock on Fridays and Saturdays during SNHA's Boat Tour Season. View the schedule to see cruise availability. Departure time changes depending on the summer and fall season. What's included 1.5 hour evening cruise at Sunset bring aboard food and drinks freely roam and explore the historic 112-year-old tour boat have a personal boat tour by tour guide on board bring aboard BYOB alcoholic beverages play music on the bluetooth speaker system Ticket Cost Tickets cost $50 per person. Due to popularity, advance reservations are advised! The cost of each ticket goes directly toward care, maintenance, storage, and tour operations of the Chief Uncas. Passenger Guidelines Passengers must be capable of navigating the boat ramp, dock, and boarding the Chief Uncas. Passengers must navigate a staircase of 3 metal grated stairs with handrail to reach the height of the boat’s entrance. Then passengers must navigate the 3 step ladder into the boat with assistance of handrails. SNHA's Crew and Captain are always present to provide additional assistance with boarding. Per US Coastguard recommendation children must be at least 6 months old to experience a tour aboard the Chief Uncas. SNHA reserves the right to deny service to individuals or groups in the interest of their own safety or the safety of other passengers, and to any person whose behavior is unacceptable, intrusive, or dangerous to other persons. Every Friday and Saturday evening

When the band’s members crossed paths on Shakedown Street, something clicked – and the music hasn’t stopped since. Rather than imitating the Dead, Shakedown Citi channels their spirit – creating spontaneous, soulful performances that feel alive, adventurous and totally in the moment. Each set is a journey, full of unexpected twists, deep grooves and musical conversation that pulls even the most skeptical listener into the vibe. Every Shakedown Citi show begins long before the first note. Each setlist is thoughtfully and meticulously crafted from the Dead repertoire, affiliated catalogs and beyond, balancing deep cuts and beloved anthems, rarities and reprises. No two nights are ever the same – each performance stands as a work of art on its own, alive in its moment, while also fitting into the larger patchwork of the repertoire. It’s not just a tribute – it’s the Dead, reborn.

events.title: Small Town Titans
events.description: Doors | 7:00 PM Show | 8:00 PM General Admission Standing Room | $29.55 + Fees Reserved Balcony & Mezzanine Seating | $40.30 + Fees +$5 on All Day of Show Purchases This event is all ages – 21+ With Valid ID to Drink Come hungry! Snacks and light bites will be available at the canteen. ————————————————— Presented by Big Fan Presents ————————————————— The Small Town Titans return to Mickey’s Black Box for their annual Home Town Holiday Show! The Small Town Titans are an American rock n’ roll power trio from York, PA who love to constantly create, as well as play live. Gone is the notion that a rock band should only release 10 songs at a time every 2 years. In a world where music fans crave new content constantly, the Small Town Titans aim to deliver their brand of art all of the time, drawing inspiration from a newer wave of rock bands such as Highly Suspect and Royal Blood, and rock legends such as the Foo Fighters, Audioslave, and Deep Purple. Thanks to their efforts at taking matters into their own hands, STT can create and release songs, podcasts, live online concerts, and more with no rules. In a social media driven world, STT knows releasing quality, constant content is as important as playing great live shows. In November of 2018, the band’s cover of the Christmas song “You’re a Mean One, Mr. Grinch” went viral in a matter of days, leading to charting on various Billboard charts including Holiday Digital Song Sales, Rock Digital Song Sales, Emerging Artists, and reaching #5 on the Next Big Sound chart. The song also reached #2 on the iTunes Rock charts, only being surpassed by Queen’s “Bohemian Rhapsody”. STT quickly found themselves achieving success, all on their own terms. As a continued unsigned act, all three members have risen to the occasion to continue to make music the way they want to, free from having to follow traditional music industry rules. By changing their mindset and focus towards creating content like many successful YouTubers, STT has made fans the old fashioned way, by word of mouth. With no manager, label, or radio support, the Small Town Titans have managed to find success by simply never forgetting one thing, their fans, both new and old. Instead of trying to make a million fans, STT is focusing on the fans they already have, and the ones they continue to make. With a love for playing live, a Small Town Titans show has evolved into more than a concert. It’s an event, with a set list that’s decided right before the show, and plenty of stage banter in between songs. The band simply hits the stage to deliver an energy driven show using guitars, drums, and their voices. Nothing more, nothing less. This approach to their live performances has led to them sharing the stage with acts such as Highly Suspect, Papa Roach, Black Stone Cherry, Pop Evil, and more. Supported By: New Damage & Common Reactor

events.title: Amish Butter Churning at Old Windmill Farm
events.description: Experience a Lancaster County tradition firsthand at Old Windmill Farm, an authentic working Amish farm in Ronks, PA. During this hands-on experience, you’ll learn how to churn fresh cream into butter using a tradition that has been passed down through generations of the family. The cream comes from the farm’s own cows, giving you a closer look at the connection between farming, food and everyday Amish life in Lancaster County. Once the butter is finished, enjoy a taste with crackers and lemonade before taking home a half-pound of freshly churned butter per person. It’s a simple, memorable way for families, couples and curious travelers to experience Amish Country beyond the roadside views.More Things to Do at Old Windmill FarmTake an Amish Farm Tour – Milk a cow, bottle feed calves, gather eggs, meet farm animals and enjoy a hayride around the property.Try the Amish Farm Fun Combo – Add seasonal gardening activities, including planting or harvesting fresh vegetables to take home.Meet & Cuddle Farm Animals – Get up close with goats, piglets, chicks, bunnies, calves and other animals, depending on the season.Book a Seasonal Farm Experience – Fall offerings can include baking bread, churning butter and pressing fresh apple cider in the farmhouse kitchen.Shop Farm-Fresh Goods – Stop by Windmill Harvest for items like raw milk, cheese, meat and canned goods to take home. Learn More about Old Windmill Farm Make a weekend of your visit! Old Windmill Farm is located in the heart of Lancaster County’s Amish countryside, close to restaurants, lodging and other popular attractions in Ronks, Paradise and Strasburg. Where to Eat Near Old Windmill Farm Make your Amish Country visit even more memorable with a meal nearby. events.description: Watch the Sunset over the Susquehanna! 1.5 hour Sunset Cruises give small groups (up to 16 passengers) the chance to roam the historic Chief Uncas for a personalized relaxing evening experience. events.title: The Amish Outlaws
events.description: Doors | 7:00 PM Show | 8:00 PM General Admission Standing Room | $32.65 + Fees Reserved Balcony & Mezzanine Seating | $37.75 + Fees +$5 on All Day of Show Purchases Please note this event is 21+ – Valid ID Required to Drink Come hungry! Snacks and light bites will be available at the canteen. ————————————————– Presented by Mickey’s Black Box ————————————————– It is a little-known fact that most Amish practice a tradition similar to the Christian “Confirmation” and Jewish “Bar Mitzvah” called “Rumspringa” (literal translation: “running around”) in which Amish children at the age of 16 have an opportunity to live free of the strict Amish code of conduct before deciding if they want to come back and be baptized into the Amish church. Surprisingly, virtually all of the youths return. But sometimes they don’t. Four out of the original six members of The Amish Outlaws were born and raised in Lancaster, PA and had a strict Amish upbringing. No electricity from land lines, no alcohol, no musical instruments, but their spirits were too wild for the Amish lifestyle. Once they trampled in the Devil’s Playground, there was no turning back. In the years since Rumspringa, the members of the Amish Outlaws have become very well acclimated to the pleasures and vices of the modern world… music, most of all. Hip hop, rock, country, metal, disco, opera. There is no genre they do not touch upon. Thus, with a bold lust for life and a fire for music and performance that can only come from 16 years of repression, The Amish Outlaws were unleashed upon the world.

events.title: Manheim Township Holiday Open House (47th Annual)
events.description: The holidays are just around the corner, and one of Manheim Township's favorite seasonal traditions is ready to make its return! The Manheim Township Recreation Department invites the community to celebrate the season at the 47th Annual Holiday Open House on Sunday, December 6, from 1:00 to 3:00 p.m. at Stauffer Mansion, located at 1241 Lititz Pike. This free, family-friendly event promises an afternoon filled with holiday entertainment, activities, and plenty of seasonal cheer. The historic mansion will come alive with festive sights and sounds throughout the afternoon. This year's entertainment lineup features performances by the Danse-Sations Youth Program at 1:05 p.m., followed by an exciting magic show with Eddie Ray Magic at 1:45 p.m. The Manheim Township High School Troubadours Choral Ensemble will round out the entertainment at 2:30 p.m., filling the mansion with holiday music. There's plenty more to enjoy between performances! Children can get creative with holiday arts and crafts from 1:15 to 2:45 p.m., while refreshments will be available throughout the event. And, of course, no holiday celebration would be complete without a visit from Santa Claus, who will be stopping by from 1:30 to 2:45 p.m. for some special holiday memories. “Whether you're grabbing a cup of hot coco, enjoying live entertainment, or getting pictures with Santa, this event is a great way to start celebrating the season,” said Manheim Township Recreation Manager Chaley Bulla. “We hope to see you Sunday, December 6th for our annual Holiday Open House!" The spirit of the season extends beyond the festivities. Manheim Township Recreation is once again partnering with Manheim Township Police and Fire Rescue to support Toys for Tots. Community members are encouraged to bring a new, unwrapped toy or non-perishable food item to donate. A collection box will be available at Stauffer Mansion during the event. Bring the family, enjoy the festivities, and make new memories at a tradition that has brought the Manheim Township community together for 47 years!

events.title: Wood Shop Tour
events.description: Watch master craftsmen handcrafting custom solid hardwood furniture. At George's, you’ll be transported to a different world where furniture is made by hand. Skilled craftsmen take a solid piece of cherry, oak, maple or walnut and carve it into furniture that is a functional work of art for your home. Each piece created is one-of-a kind, signed and dated by the artisan. Enjoy watching handmade furniture being built, and shop in our showroom. Woodshop Tour Hours Mon-Fri, 9 a.m.-2 p.m. Showroom hours Mon-Sat 9am–5pm. Our tour begins in our showroom where we learn about the 50+ year history of Georges furniture, from hobby to business, what makes George's different from other furniture stores, and the amazing ability of our extension tables. (Tables start at 5 ft and extend to 12+ feet with ease.) then proceed to our wood working shop where the craftsmen select the wood looking at the grain, using basic saws, jointers, sanders and planers. Next, we see the furniture be stained and protected with a water-resistant finish. Finally we see our showroom with our 21-foot dining table and our bedroom furniture. After our wood shop tour, people look at furniture a whole new way. It is very informative and impactful. Monday-Friday weekly from 9-2pm year round

events.description: Join us for this beloved annual event as we celebrate America 250, Lititz 270, and Lititz Historical Foundation’s 65th anniversaries! Two very merry nights! Our popular Annual Christmas Candlelight Tour is back, and this time, will take place over two nights! What better way to get into the holiday spirit than to visit Lititz, Pennsylvania. On December 12th and 13th, the Lititz Historical Foundation will hold its Annual Christmas Candlelight Tour. Guests will receive a guided tour of the 1792 Johannes Mueller House and will learn the story of Mueller and his family as well as history and customs of the early Moravian community of Lititz during the 18th century. Tours depart every 15 minutes and run from 5-8pm each evening. While you’re there, be sure to visit the Lititz Museum for holiday refreshments and to shop our gift shop for a tremendous selection of items! events.title: Wood Shop Tour
events.description: Watch master craftsmen handcrafting custom solid hardwood furniture. At George's, you’ll be transported to a different world where furniture is made by hand. Skilled craftsmen take a solid piece of cherry, oak, maple or walnut and carve it into furniture that is a functional work of art for your home. Each piece created is one-of-a kind, signed and dated by the artisan. Enjoy watching handmade furniture being built, and shop in our showroom. Woodshop Tour Hours Mon-Fri, 9 a.m.-2 p.m. Showroom hours Mon-Sat 9am–5pm. Our tour begins in our showroom where we learn about the 50+ year history of Georges furniture, from hobby to business, what makes George's different from other furniture stores, and the amazing ability of our extension tables. (Tables start at 5 ft and extend to 12+ feet with ease.) then proceed to our wood working shop where the craftsmen select the wood looking at the grain, using basic saws, jointers, sanders and planers. Next, we see the furniture be stained and protected with a water-resistant finish. Finally we see our showroom with our 21-foot dining table and our bedroom furniture. After our wood shop tour, people look at furniture a whole new way. It is very informative and impactful. Monday-Friday weekly from 9-2pm year round

events.title: Amish Butter Churning at Old Windmill Farm
events.description: Experience a Lancaster County tradition firsthand at Old Windmill Farm, an authentic working Amish farm in Ronks, PA. During this hands-on experience, you’ll learn how to churn fresh cream into butter using a tradition that has been passed down through generations of the family. The cream comes from the farm’s own cows, giving you a closer look at the connection between farming, food and everyday Amish life in Lancaster County. Once the butter is finished, enjoy a taste with crackers and lemonade before taking home a half-pound of freshly churned butter per person. It’s a simple, memorable way for families, couples and curious travelers to experience Amish Country beyond the roadside views.More Things to Do at Old Windmill FarmTake an Amish Farm Tour – Milk a cow, bottle feed calves, gather eggs, meet farm animals and enjoy a hayride around the property.Try the Amish Farm Fun Combo – Add seasonal gardening activities, including planting or harvesting fresh vegetables to take home.Meet & Cuddle Farm Animals – Get up close with goats, piglets, chicks, bunnies, calves and other animals, depending on the season.Book a Seasonal Farm Experience – Fall offerings can include baking bread, churning butter and pressing fresh apple cider in the farmhouse kitchen.Shop Farm-Fresh Goods – Stop by Windmill Harvest for items like raw milk, cheese, meat and canned goods to take home. Learn More about Old Windmill Farm Make a weekend of your visit! Old Windmill Farm is located in the heart of Lancaster County’s Amish countryside, close to restaurants, lodging and other popular attractions in Ronks, Paradise and Strasburg. Where to Eat Near Old Windmill Farm Make your Amish Country visit even more memorable with a meal nearby. Hershey Farm Grand Smorgasbord – Enjoy Pennsylvania Dutch favorites, homestyle dishes, baked goods and a full smorgasbord experience. Dienner’s Country Restaurant – A local favorite for traditional Pennsylvania Dutch comfort food, homemade dishes and buffet selections. Miller’s Smorgasbord – Experience a Lancaster County tradition with a wide selection of Pennsylvania Dutch dishes, carved meats, fresh baked desserts and more. Fireside Tavern – For something a little different, head to nearby Strasburg for steaks, seafood, sandwiches and casual American fare in a cozy tavern setting. More Places to Eat in Lancaster Places to Stay Near Old Windmill Farm Turn your butter-churning experience into an overnight getaway and spend more time exploring Lancaster County’s Amish countryside. Hershey Farm Resort – Relax on a scenic Amish Country property featuring charming guest rooms, countryside views, walking paths, an outdoor pool, and on-site Smorgasbord, gift shop, bakery, and cafe. The Red Caboose Motel at Paradise Station – Spend the night in a restored railroad caboose surrounded by Lancaster County farmland for a stay that’s especially fun for families and train lovers. Fulton Steamboat Inn – A distinctive steamboat-themed hotel with an indoor pool, on-site dining and a convenient location near attractions throughout the Route 30 and Strasburg area. The Cabins at Beaver Creek – Settle into a private cabin surrounded by the peaceful Lancaster County countryside for a quieter, more relaxed Amish Country getaway. More Places to Stay in Lancaster

events.title: Chief Uncas Sunset Cruise
events.description: Watch the Sunset over the Susquehanna! 1.5 hour Sunset Cruises give small groups (up to 16 passengers) the chance to roam the historic Chief Uncas for a personalized relaxing evening experience. Bring aboard food and B.Y.O.B. alcoholic beverages to enjoy as the Chief Uncas silently cruises under the setting sun. Store your cold drinks in the vintage ice box and use the boat’s Bluetooth speakers to play your favorite music. A knowledgeable crew member is aboard as your guide to answer questions or give a tour of the river. The perfect experience for a date night or fun time with friends! Sunset Cruises depart from the Zimmerman Center dock on Fridays and Saturdays during SNHA's Boat Tour Season. View the schedule to see cruise availability. Departure time changes depending on the summer and fall season. What's included 1.5 hour evening cruise at Sunset bring aboard food and drinks freely roam and explore the historic 112-year-old tour boat have a personal boat tour by tour guide on board bring aboard BYOB alcoholic beverages play music on the bluetooth speaker system Ticket Cost Tickets cost $50 per person. Due to popularity, advance reservations are advised! The cost of each ticket goes directly toward care, maintenance, storage, and tour operations of the Chief Uncas. Passenger Guidelines Passengers must be capable of navigating the boat ramp, dock, and boarding the Chief Uncas. Passengers must navigate a staircase of 3 metal grated stairs with handrail to reach the height of the boat’s entrance. Then passengers must navigate the 3 step ladder into the boat with assistance of handrails. SNHA's Crew and Captain are always present to provide additional assistance with boarding. Per US Coastguard recommendation children must be at least 6 months old to experience a tour aboard the Chief Uncas. SNHA reserves the right to deny service to individuals or groups in the interest of their own safety or the safety of other passengers, and to any person whose behavior is unacceptable, intrusive, or dangerous to other persons. Every Friday and Saturday evening

events.description: Watch the Sunset over the Susquehanna! 1.5 hour Sunset Cruises give small groups (up to 16 passengers) the chance to roam the historic Chief Uncas for a personalized relaxing evening experience. Bring aboard food and B.Y.O.B. alcoholic beverages to enjoy as the Chief Uncas silently cruises under the setting sun. Store your cold drinks in the vintage ice box and use the boat’s Bluetooth speakers to play your favorite music. A knowledgeable crew member is aboard as your guide to answer questions or give a tour of the river. The perfect experience for a date night or fun time with friends! Sunset Cruises depart from the Zimmerman Center dock on Fridays and Saturdays during SNHA's Boat Tour Season. View the schedule to see cruise availability. Departure time changes depending on the summer and fall season. What's included 1.5 hour evening cruise at Sunset bring aboard food and drinks freely roam and explore the historic 112-year-old tour boat have a personal boat tour by tour guide on board bring aboard BYOB alcoholic beverages play music on the bluetooth speaker system Ticket Cost Tickets cost $50 per person. Due to popularity, advance reservations are advised! The cost of each ticket goes directly toward care, maintenance, storage, and tour operations of the Chief Uncas. Passenger Guidelines Passengers must be capable of navigating the boat ramp, dock, and boarding the Chief Uncas. Passengers must navigate a staircase of 3 metal grated stairs with handrail to reach the height of the boat’s entrance. Then passengers must navigate the 3 step ladder into the boat with assistance of handrails. SNHA's Crew and Captain are always present to provide additional assistance with boarding. Per US Coastguard recommendation children must be at least 6 months old to experience a tour aboard the Chief Uncas. SNHA reserves the right to deny service to individuals or groups in the interest of their own safety or the safety of other passengers, and to any person whose behavior is unacceptable, intrusive, or dangerous to other persons. Every Friday and Saturday evening

Ever since forming in New Jersey in 2001, the band, now consisting of frontman Ace Enders and founding drummer Jeff Kummer— have constantly been striving to find the best and most definitive version of themselves. events.title: Wood Shop Tour
events.description: Watch master craftsmen handcrafting custom solid hardwood furniture. At George's, you’ll be transported to a different world where furniture is made by hand. Skilled craftsmen take a solid piece of cherry, oak, maple or walnut and carve it into furniture that is a functional work of art for your home. Each piece created is one-of-a kind, signed and dated by the artisan. Enjoy watching handmade furniture being built, and shop in our showroom. Woodshop Tour Hours Mon-Fri, 9 a.m.-2 p.m. Showroom hours Mon-Sat 9am–5pm. Our tour begins in our showroom where we learn about the 50+ year history of Georges furniture, from hobby to business, what makes George's different from other furniture stores, and the amazing ability of our extension tables. (Tables start at 5 ft and extend to 12+ feet with ease.) then proceed to our wood working shop where the craftsmen select the wood looking at the grain, using basic saws, jointers, sanders and planers. Next, we see the furniture be stained and protected with a water-resistant finish. Finally we see our showroom with our 21-foot dining table and our bedroom furniture. After our wood shop tour, people look at furniture a whole new way. It is very informative and impactful. Monday-Friday weekly from 9-2pm year round

Skilled craftsmen take a solid piece of cherry, oak, maple or walnut and carve it into furniture that is a functional work of art for your home. Each piece created is one-of-a kind, signed and dated by the artisan. Enjoy watching handmade furniture being built, and shop in our showroom. Woodshop Tour Hours Mon-Fri, 9 a.m.-2 p.m. Showroom hours Mon-Sat 9am–5pm. Our tour begins in our showroom where we learn about the 50+ year history of Georges furniture, from hobby to business, what makes George's different from other furniture stores, and the amazing ability of our extension tables. (Tables start at 5 ft and extend to 12+ feet with ease.) then proceed to our wood working shop where the craftsmen select the wood looking at the grain, using basic saws, jointers, sanders and planers. Next, we see the furniture be stained and protected with a water-resistant finish. Finally we see our showroom with our 21-foot dining table and our bedroom furniture. After our wood shop tour, people look at furniture a whole new way. It is very informative and impactful. Monday-Friday weekly from 9-2pm year round

events.title: Amish Butter Churning at Old Windmill Farm
events.description: Experience a Lancaster County tradition firsthand at Old Windmill Farm, an authentic working Amish farm in Ronks, PA. During this hands-on experience, you’ll learn how to churn fresh cream into butter using a tradition that has been passed down through generations of the family. The cream comes from the farm’s own cows, giving you a closer look at the connection between farming, food and everyday Amish life in Lancaster County. Once the butter is finished, enjoy a taste with crackers and lemonade before taking home a half-pound of freshly churned butter per person. It’s a simple, memorable way for families, couples and curious travelers to experience Amish Country beyond the roadside views.More Things to Do at Old Windmill FarmTake an Amish Farm Tour – Milk a cow, bottle feed calves, gather eggs, meet farm animals and enjoy a hayride around the property.Try the Amish Farm Fun Combo – Add seasonal gardening activities, including planting or harvesting fresh vegetables to take home.Meet & Cuddle Farm Animals – Get up close with goats, piglets, chicks, bunnies, calves and other animals, depending on the season.Book a Seasonal Farm Experience – Fall offerings can include baking bread, churning butter and pressing fresh apple cider in the farmhouse kitchen.Shop Farm-Fresh Goods – Stop by Windmill Harvest for items like raw milk, cheese, meat and canned goods to take home. Learn More about Old Windmill Farm Make a weekend of your visit! Old Windmill Farm is located in the heart of Lancaster County’s Amish countryside, close to restaurants, lodging and other popular attractions in Ronks, Paradise and Strasburg. Where to Eat Near Old Windmill Farm Make your Amish Country visit even more memorable with a meal nearby. Hershey Farm Grand Smorgasbord – Enjoy Pennsylvania Dutch favorites, homestyle dishes, baked goods and a full smorgasbord experience. Dienner’s Country Restaurant – A local favorite for traditional Pennsylvania Dutch comfort food, homemade dishes and buffet selections. Miller’s Smorgasbord – Experience a Lancaster County tradition with a wide selection of Pennsylvania Dutch dishes, carved meats, fresh baked desserts and more. Fireside Tavern – For something a little different, head to nearby Strasburg for steaks, seafood, sandwiches and casual American fare in a cozy tavern setting. More Places to Eat in Lancaster Places to Stay Near Old Windmill Farm Turn your butter-churning experience into an overnight getaway and spend more time exploring Lancaster County’s Amish countryside. Hershey Farm Resort – Relax on a scenic Amish Country property featuring charming guest rooms, countryside views, walking paths, an outdoor pool, and on-site Smorgasbord, gift shop, bakery, and cafe. The Red Caboose Motel at Paradise Station – Spend the night in a restored railroad caboose surrounded by Lancaster County farmland for a stay that’s especially fun for families and train lovers. Fulton Steamboat Inn – A distinctive steamboat-themed hotel with an indoor pool, on-site dining and a convenient location near attractions throughout the Route 30 and Strasburg area. The Cabins at Beaver Creek – Settle into a private cabin surrounded by the peaceful Lancaster County countryside for a quieter, more relaxed Amish Country getaway. More Places to Stay in Lancaster

events.title: Watercolor Club
events.description: Friday afternoon is a great time to set your intention for a grounded and restful weekend. What better way to do it than with an hour of play and relaxation with other friendly creatives.Watercolor Club low-pressure, watercolor play time for adults. Come as you are, grab your favorite supplies, and explore color, gesture, and mood. I’m on hand to answer any questions you have and provide some tips and tricks, all to help you loosen up and collaborate with the medium. Absolutely no experience needed.We meet at WestArt where you can grab some coffee or whatever suits your fancy, settle in and enjoy the vibes while being part of a vibrant and growing community of artists. Bring your favorite materials or show up empty handed, either way, I’ve got you covered.What to expect:Watercolor club is a place to explore the magic and wonder of watercolor while honing your skills at the same time. No experience necessary. If you’ve always wanted to paint with watercolor but find it frustrating, this is the place for you. If you’ve been painting with watercolor for years but want to loosen up, this is the place for you. No matter where you are with your artistic practice (or lack thereof) you’ll feel right at home.What to bring:I supply materials, but you are welcome to bring any of your own.All levels welcome. just bring yourself and a willingness to play. I hope to see you there! Every Friday afternoon

events.description: Watch the Sunset over the Susquehanna! 1.5 hour Sunset Cruises give small groups (up to 16 passengers) the chance to roam the historic Chief Uncas for a personalized relaxing evening experience. A knowledgeable crew member is aboard as your guide to answer questions or give a tour of the river. The perfect experience for a date night or fun time with friends! Sunset Cruises depart from the Zimmerman Center dock on Fridays and Saturdays during SNHA's Boat Tour Season. View the schedule to see cruise availability. Departure time changes depending on the summer and fall season. What's included 1.5 hour evening cruise at Sunset bring aboard food and drinks freely roam and explore the historic 112-year-old tour boat have a personal boat tour by tour guide on board bring aboard BYOB alcoholic beverages play music on the bluetooth speaker system Ticket Cost Tickets cost $50 per person. Due to popularity, advance reservations are advised! The cost of each ticket goes directly toward care, maintenance, storage, and tour operations of the Chief Uncas. Passenger Guidelines Passengers must be capable of navigating the boat ramp, dock, and boarding the Chief Uncas. Passengers must navigate a staircase of 3 metal grated stairs with handrail to reach the height of the boat’s entrance. Then passengers must navigate the 3 step ladder into the boat with assistance of handrails. SNHA's Crew and Captain are always present to provide additional assistance with boarding. Per US Coastguard recommendation children must be at least 6 months old to experience a tour aboard the Chief Uncas. SNHA reserves the right to deny service to individuals or groups in the interest of their own safety or the safety of other passengers, and to any person whose behavior is unacceptable, intrusive, or dangerous to other persons. Every Friday and Saturday evening

events.title: Wood Shop Tour
events.description: Watch master craftsmen handcrafting custom solid hardwood furniture. At George's, you’ll be transported to a different world where furniture is made by hand. Skilled craftsmen take a solid piece of cherry, oak, maple or walnut and carve it into furniture that is a functional work of art for your home. Each piece created is one-of-a kind, signed and dated by the artisan. Enjoy watching handmade furniture being built, and shop in our showroom. Woodshop Tour Hours Mon-Fri, 9 a.m.-2 p.m. Showroom hours Mon-Sat 9am–5pm. Our tour begins in our showroom where we learn about the 50+ year history of Georges furniture, from hobby to business, what makes George's different from other furniture stores, and the amazing ability of our extension tables. (Tables start at 5 ft and extend to 12+ feet with ease.) then proceed to our wood working shop where the craftsmen select the wood looking at the grain, using basic saws, jointers, sanders and planers. Next, we see the furniture be stained and protected with a water-resistant finish. Finally we see our showroom with our 21-foot dining table and our bedroom furniture. After our wood shop tour, people look at furniture a whole new way. It is very informative and impactful. Monday-Friday weekly from 9-2pm year round

events.title: Amish Butter Churning at Old Windmill Farm
events.description: Experience a Lancaster County tradition firsthand at Old Windmill Farm, an authentic working Amish farm in Ronks, PA. During this hands-on experience, you’ll learn how to churn fresh cream into butter using a tradition that has been passed down through generations of the family. The cream comes from the farm’s own cows, giving you a closer look at the connection between farming, food and everyday Amish life in Lancaster County. Once the butter is finished, enjoy a taste with crackers and lemonade before taking home a half-pound of freshly churned butter per person. It’s a simple, memorable way for families, couples and curious travelers to experience Amish Country beyond the roadside views.More Things to Do at Old Windmill FarmTake an Amish Farm Tour – Milk a cow, bottle feed calves, gather eggs, meet farm animals and enjoy a hayride around the property.Try the Amish Farm Fun Combo – Add seasonal gardening activities, including planting or harvesting fresh vegetables to take home.Meet & Cuddle Farm Animals – Get up close with goats, piglets, chicks, bunnies, calves and other animals, depending on the season.Book a Seasonal Farm Experience – Fall offerings can include baking bread, churning butter and pressing fresh apple cider in the farmhouse kitchen.Shop Farm-Fresh Goods – Stop by Windmill Harvest for items like raw milk, cheese, meat and canned goods to take home. Learn More about Old Windmill Farm Make a weekend of your visit! Old Windmill Farm is located in the heart of Lancaster County’s Amish countryside, close to restaurants, lodging and other popular attractions in Ronks, Paradise and Strasburg. Where to Eat Near Old Windmill Farm Make your Amish Country visit even more memorable with a meal nearby. Hershey Farm Grand Smorgasbord – Enjoy Pennsylvania Dutch favorites, homestyle dishes, baked goods and a full smorgasbord experience. Dienner’s Country Restaurant – A local favorite for traditional Pennsylvania Dutch comfort food, homemade dishes and buffet selections. Miller’s Smorgasbord – Experience a Lancaster County tradition with a wide selection of Pennsylvania Dutch dishes, carved meats, fresh baked desserts and more. Fireside Tavern – For something a little different, head to nearby Strasburg for steaks, seafood, sandwiches and casual American fare in a cozy tavern setting. More Places to Eat in Lancaster Places to Stay Near Old Windmill Farm Turn your butter-churning experience into an overnight getaway and spend more time exploring Lancaster County’s Amish countryside. Hershey Farm Resort – Relax on a scenic Amish Country property featuring charming guest rooms, countryside views, walking paths, an outdoor pool, and on-site Smorgasbord, gift shop, bakery, and cafe. The Red Caboose Motel at Paradise Station – Spend the night in a restored railroad caboose surrounded by Lancaster County farmland for a stay that’s especially fun for families and train lovers. Fulton Steamboat Inn – A distinctive steamboat-themed hotel with an indoor pool, on-site dining and a convenient location near attractions throughout the Route 30 and Strasburg area. The Cabins at Beaver Creek – Settle into a private cabin surrounded by the peaceful Lancaster County countryside for a quieter, more relaxed Amish Country getaway. More Places to Stay in Lancaster

events.title: Chief Uncas Sunset Cruise
events.description: Watch the Sunset over the Susquehanna! 1.5 hour Sunset Cruises give small groups (up to 16 passengers) the chance to roam the historic Chief Uncas for a personalized relaxing evening experience. Bring aboard food and B.Y.O.B. alcoholic beverages to enjoy as the Chief Uncas silently cruises under the setting sun. Store your cold drinks in the vintage ice box and use the boat’s Bluetooth speakers to play your favorite music. A knowledgeable crew member is aboard as your guide to answer questions or give a tour of the river. The perfect experience for a date night or fun time with friends! Sunset Cruises depart from the Zimmerman Center dock on Fridays and Saturdays during SNHA's Boat Tour Season. View the schedule to see cruise availability. Departure time changes depending on the summer and fall season. What's included 1.5 hour evening cruise at Sunset bring aboard food and drinks freely roam and explore the historic 112-year-old tour boat have a personal boat tour by tour guide on board bring aboard BYOB alcoholic beverages play music on the bluetooth speaker system Ticket Cost Tickets cost $50 per person. Due to popularity, advance reservations are advised! The cost of each ticket goes directly toward care, maintenance, storage, and tour operations of the Chief Uncas. Passenger Guidelines Passengers must be capable of navigating the boat ramp, dock, and boarding the Chief Uncas. Passengers must navigate a staircase of 3 metal grated stairs with handrail to reach the height of the boat’s entrance. Then passengers must navigate the 3 step ladder into the boat with assistance of handrails. SNHA's Crew and Captain are always present to provide additional assistance with boarding. Per US Coastguard recommendation children must be at least 6 months old to experience a tour aboard the Chief Uncas. SNHA reserves the right to deny service to individuals or groups in the interest of their own safety or the safety of other passengers, and to any person whose behavior is unacceptable, intrusive, or dangerous to other persons. Every Friday and Saturday evening

events.title: Amish Butter Churning at Old Windmill Farm
events.description: Experience a Lancaster County tradition firsthand at Old Windmill Farm, an authentic working Amish farm in Ronks, PA. During this hands-on experience, you’ll learn how to churn fresh cream into butter using a tradition that has been passed down through generations of the family. The cream comes from the farm’s own cows, giving you a closer look at the connection between farming, food and everyday Amish life in Lancaster County. Once the butter is finished, enjoy a taste with crackers and lemonade before taking home a half-pound of freshly churned butter per person. It’s a simple, memorable way for families, couples and curious travelers to experience Amish Country beyond the roadside views.More Things to Do at Old Windmill FarmTake an Amish Farm Tour – Milk a cow, bottle feed calves, gather eggs, meet farm animals and enjoy a hayride around the property.Try the Amish Farm Fun Combo – Add seasonal gardening activities, including planting or harvesting fresh vegetables to take home.Meet & Cuddle Farm Animals – Get up close with goats, piglets, chicks, bunnies, calves and other animals, depending on the season.Book a Seasonal Farm Experience – Fall offerings can include baking bread, churning butter and pressing fresh apple cider in the farmhouse kitchen.Shop Farm-Fresh Goods – Stop by Windmill Harvest for items like raw milk, cheese, meat and canned goods to take home. Learn More about Old Windmill Farm Make a weekend of your visit! Old Windmill Farm is located in the heart of Lancaster County’s Amish countryside, close to restaurants, lodging and other popular attractions in Ronks, Paradise and Strasburg. events.title: Chief Uncas Sunset Cruise
events.description: Watch the Sunset over the Susquehanna! 1.5 hour Sunset Cruises give small groups (up to 16 passengers) the chance to roam the historic Chief Uncas for a personalized relaxing evening experience. Bring aboard food and B.Y.O.B. alcoholic beverages to enjoy as the Chief Uncas silently cruises under the setting sun. Store your cold drinks in the vintage ice box and use the boat’s Bluetooth speakers to play your favorite music. A knowledgeable crew member is aboard as your guide to answer questions or give a tour of the river. The perfect experience for a date night or fun time with friends! Sunset Cruises depart from the Zimmerman Center dock on Fridays and Saturdays during SNHA's Boat Tour Season. View the schedule to see cruise availability. Departure time changes depending on the summer and fall season. What's included 1.5 hour evening cruise at Sunset bring aboard food and drinks freely roam and explore the historic 112-year-old tour boat have a personal boat tour by tour guide on board bring aboard BYOB alcoholic beverages play music on the bluetooth speaker system Ticket Cost Tickets cost $50 per person. Due to popularity, advance reservations are advised! The cost of each ticket goes directly toward care, maintenance, storage, and tour operations of the Chief Uncas. Passenger Guidelines Passengers must be capable of navigating the boat ramp, dock, and boarding the Chief Uncas. Passengers must navigate a staircase of 3 metal grated stairs with handrail to reach the height of the boat’s entrance. Then passengers must navigate the 3 step ladder into the boat with assistance of handrails. SNHA's Crew and Captain are always present to provide additional assistance with boarding. Per US Coastguard recommendation children must be at least 6 months old to experience a tour aboard the Chief Uncas. SNHA reserves the right to deny service to individuals or groups in the interest of their own safety or the safety of other passengers, and to any person whose behavior is unacceptable, intrusive, or dangerous to other persons. Every Friday and Saturday evening

events.title: Living the Experience
events.description: Living the Experience is a spiritual, interactive reenactment of the Underground railroad. Patrons get a chance to step inside the shoes of Africans seeking their freedom in the 1800's in Lancaster, Pennsylvania. The production is the first Underground Railroad reenactment in Central Pennsylvania and has been sharing the story for 27 years. Each includes our reenactment, a southern style meal and access to local vendors on site. At our October 4th production you will also get a chance to meet award winning storyteller and former Jeopardy! cast member, Cheryl Farrell. She will be explaining how the Historical Bethel A.M.E. Church was featured on the popular game show and the importance of storytelling in the African heritage. Ticket sales end 1 week before each production. Groups of 35 or more may reserve a different date upon request. Please contact us for more information. Immerse yourself into history like never before. Come Live the Experience! This event happens every 1st Saturday

Snacks and light bites will be available at the canteen. ————————————————– Presented by Mickey’s Black Box ————————————————– BLURRYFACE is a tribute to Twenty One Pilots built by fans, for fans. Designed to capture the energy, emotion, and spectacle of a full Twenty One Pilots concert, BLURRYFACE delivers an up-close and personal live experience crafted specifically for intimate venues where the original band cultivated their passionate fanbase. Audiences get the rare feeling of being fully immersed in the music, the visuals, and the community that has made Twenty One Pilots one of modern music’s most dedicated fanbases. This is far more than a cover set. BLURRYFACE recreates the feeling of a modern Twenty One Pilots arena production inside a smaller, more personal environment. Featuring synchronized video content, dynamic lighting, programmed visuals, CO2 cannons, and carefully curated live moments, every aspect of the show is designed to capture the emotional highs, explosive energy, and atmosphere fans know and love. From massive singalongs to intimate moments of reflection, the goal is to make every audience member feel like they are part of something bigger than just a concert. At its core, BLURRYFACE exists to celebrate the music and the community surrounding it. The members of BLURRYFACE are massive Twenty One Pilots fans themselves, with a deep understanding of the connection this music creates for people. The band is not trying to imitate or pretend to be Twenty One Pilots. Instead, they aim to honor the experience that Tyler and Josh created by bringing fans together in a safe, welcoming environment where they can express themselves freely, celebrate the music they love, and share in the emotional connection that has always been at the heart of the Twenty One Pilots community.

events.title: Jeff Allen at The Junction Center
events.description: About the Tour: The Love and Laughter Tour Jeff’s show features his brilliant standup comedy, which has garnered hundreds of millions of fans around the globe. There is a part of Jeff’s show where he speaks about his book, Are We There Yet? which tears down all walls and shows Jeff’s journey from very dark times to recovery, restoration, and ultimately redemption. For those inspired by Jeff’s arc, thistour is more than just laughs – it’s about hope, healing, and making a difference. Jeff’s mission statement is Tikkun Olam, a Hebrew phrase meaning “Repairing the World.” His goal is simple: “I want to make a difference that outlives the tour… that outlives me.” Jeff Allen’s Bio Jeff Allen is one of America’s most beloved comedians, with over one billion online views. His rapid-fire humor, which centers on marriage and family, is a hit with all ages. He has appeared everywhere – on Comedy Central, Showtime, TBN, CBN, Family Net, Dry Bar Comedy (their most viewed comedian with seven comedy specials), America’s Got Talent, HBO, Amazon Prime, Huckabee, Pureflix, VH-1, The Today Show, and starred in the films Apostles of Comedy and My 7 Grandmas. He has performed for our troops on aircraft carriers and shipsin the Indian Ocean. Jeff has also performed at three Presidential Inaugural Galas. Millions have seen him across Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, and YouTube. But nothing compares to seeing Jeff live. He is presently in pre-production for his new series based on his book, Are We There Yet? Accessible seating is available on the main floor. For questions and accommodations, please contact boxoffice@thejunctioncenter.com or call 717-459-3701 iTickets is the official ticketing provider for this event. To ensure valid entry and receive the most up-to-date event information, all tickets should be purchased through iTickets or by calling The Junction Center directly.

events.description: Watch the Sunset over the Susquehanna! 1.5 hour Sunset Cruises give small groups (up to 16 passengers) the chance to roam the historic Chief Uncas for a personalized relaxing evening experience. Bring aboard food and B.Y.O.B. alcoholic beverages to enjoy as the Chief Uncas silently cruises under the setting sun. Store your cold drinks in the vintage ice box and use the boat’s Bluetooth speakers to play your favorite music. A knowledgeable crew member is aboard as your guide to answer questions or give a tour of the river. The perfect experience for a date night or fun time with friends! Sunset Cruises depart from the Zimmerman Center dock on Fridays and Saturdays during SNHA's Boat Tour Season. View the schedule to see cruise availability. Departure time changes depending on the summer and fall season. What's included 1.5 hour evening cruise at Sunset bring aboard food and drinks freely roam and explore the historic 112-year-old tour boat have a personal boat tour by tour guide on board bring aboard BYOB alcoholic beverages play music on the bluetooth speaker system Ticket Cost Tickets cost $50 per person. Due to popularity, advance reservations are advised! The cost of each ticket goes directly toward care, maintenance, storage, and tour operations of the Chief Uncas. Passenger Guidelines Passengers must be capable of navigating the boat ramp, dock, and boarding the Chief Uncas. Passengers must navigate a staircase of 3 metal grated stairs with handrail to reach the height of the boat’s entrance. Then passengers must navigate the 3 step ladder into the boat with assistance of handrails. SNHA's Crew and Captain are always present to provide additional assistance with boarding. Per US Coastguard recommendation children must be at least 6 months old to experience a tour aboard the Chief Uncas. SNHA reserves the right to deny service to individuals or groups in the interest of their own safety or the safety of other passengers, and to any person whose behavior is unacceptable, intrusive, or dangerous to other persons. Every Friday and Saturday evening

events.title: Tales & Legends
events.description: Join the Lancaster Symphony Orhcestra! Music's greatest storytellers take center stage in a program dedicated to the art of musical narrative. Wagner's grand Prelude to Die Meistersinger opens with themes of mastery and tradition, followed by the world premiere of Austin Wintory's Interactive Concerto for Guitar featuring 4-time Grammy-nominated guitarist Mak Grgić in an innovative new work that bridges classical and contemporary worlds. The concert concludes with Rimsky-Korsakov's enchanting Scheherazade—the ultimate musical storyteller—spinning tales from the Arabian Nights with exotic melodies, shimmering orchestration, and the seductive voice of the solo violin. From European legends to interactive innovation to Arabian tales, this concert celebrates music's timeless power to tell extraordinary stories.

events.title: Amish Butter Churning at Old Windmill Farm
events.description: Experience a Lancaster County tradition firsthand at Old Windmill Farm, an authentic working Amish farm in Ronks, PA. During this hands-on experience, you’ll learn how to churn fresh cream into butter using a tradition that has been passed down through generations of the family. The cream comes from the farm’s own cows, giving you a closer look at the connection between farming, food and everyday Amish life in Lancaster County. Once the butter is finished, enjoy a taste with crackers and lemonade before taking home a half-pound of freshly churned butter per person. It’s a simple, memorable way for families, couples and curious travelers to experience Amish Country beyond the roadside views.More Things to Do at Old Windmill FarmTake an Amish Farm Tour – Milk a cow, bottle feed calves, gather eggs, meet farm animals and enjoy a hayride around the property.Try the Amish Farm Fun Combo – Add seasonal gardening activities, including planting or harvesting fresh vegetables to take home.Meet & Cuddle Farm Animals – Get up close with goats, piglets, chicks, bunnies, calves and other animals, depending on the season.Book a Seasonal Farm Experience – Fall offerings can include baking bread, churning butter and pressing fresh apple cider in the farmhouse kitchen.Shop Farm-Fresh Goods – Stop by Windmill Harvest for items like raw milk, cheese, meat and canned goods to take home. Learn More about Old Windmill Farm Make a weekend of your visit! Old Windmill Farm is located in the heart of Lancaster County’s Amish countryside, close to restaurants, lodging and other popular attractions in Ronks, Paradise and Strasburg. Where to Eat Near Old Windmill Farm Make your Amish Country visit even more memorable with a meal nearby. Hershey Farm Grand Smorgasbord – Enjoy Pennsylvania Dutch favorites, homestyle dishes, baked goods and a full smorgasbord experience. Dienner’s Country Restaurant – A local favorite for traditional Pennsylvania Dutch comfort food, homemade dishes and buffet selections. Miller’s Smorgasbord – Experience a Lancaster County tradition with a wide selection of Pennsylvania Dutch dishes, carved meats, fresh baked desserts and more. Fireside Tavern – For something a little different, head to nearby Strasburg for steaks, seafood, sandwiches and casual American fare in a cozy tavern setting. More Places to Eat in Lancaster Places to Stay Near Old Windmill Farm Turn your butter-churning experience into an overnight getaway and spend more time exploring Lancaster County’s Amish countryside. Hershey Farm Resort – Relax on a scenic Amish Country property featuring charming guest rooms, countryside views, walking paths, an outdoor pool, and on-site Smorgasbord, gift shop, bakery, and cafe. The Red Caboose Motel at Paradise Station – Spend the night in a restored railroad caboose surrounded by Lancaster County farmland for a stay that’s especially fun for families and train lovers. Fulton Steamboat Inn – A distinctive steamboat-themed hotel with an indoor pool, on-site dining and a convenient location near attractions throughout the Route 30 and Strasburg area. The Cabins at Beaver Creek – Settle into a private cabin surrounded by the peaceful Lancaster County countryside for a quieter, more relaxed Amish Country getaway. More Places to Stay in Lancaster

events.description: Friday afternoon is a great time to set your intention for a grounded and restful weekend. What better way to do it than with an hour of play and relaxation with other friendly creatives.Watercolor Club low-pressure, watercolor play time for adults. Come as you are, grab your favorite supplies, and explore color, gesture, and mood. I’m on hand to answer any questions you have and provide some tips and tricks, all to help you loosen up and collaborate with the medium. Absolutely no experience needed.We meet at WestArt where you can grab some coffee or whatever suits your fancy, settle in and enjoy the vibes while being part of a vibrant and growing community of artists. Bring your favorite materials or show up empty handed, either way, I’ve got you covered.What to expect:Watercolor club is a place to explore the magic and wonder of watercolor while honing your skills at the same time. events.title: Dominate the Storm: A Heart Pumping Evening with Reed Timmer, America's Most Famous Storm Chaser
events.description: Experience the raw power of nature through the eyes of Dr. Reed Timmer, extreme meteorologist, scientist, and one of the world’s most renowned storm chasers. With a PhD in meteorology from the University of Oklahoma, Reed has devoted his life to intercepting the planet’s most dangerous storms, collecting groundbreaking scientific data, and helping audiences better understand how severe weather is changing. Over the past several decades, Reed has intercepted more than 1,000 tornadoes and 50 hurricanes, including EF5 tornadoes and Category 5 hurricanes. He is also the inventor of the Dominators—armored, tank-like storm-chasing vehicles equipped with advanced meteorological sensors, hydraulic anchoring spikes, drones, probes, balloons, and even model rockets. Since 2020, Reed has driven Dominator 3 directly into 10 tornadoes, more than any other person in history. His unforgettable expeditions include recording 140 mph winds from inside a Nebraska tornado and launching a trackable sensor into a mile-wide EF4 tornado in Kansas. Carried as high as 39,000 feet and reaching speeds of 190 mph, the sensor captured unprecedented data throughout its 30-mile journey inside the vortex. Currently chasing storms for the National Geographic Channel and RadarOmega, Reed also provides vital real-time reports through traditional and social media. Hear the incredible stories, witness breathtaking footage, and discover the science behind Earth’s most powerful storms during this heart-pumping live event. For Reed Timmer, “Never Stop Chasing” is more than a motto—it is a way of life.

events.title: Amish Butter Churning at Old Windmill Farm
events.description: Experience a Lancaster County tradition firsthand at Old Windmill Farm, an authentic working Amish farm in Ronks, PA. During this hands-on experience, you’ll learn how to churn fresh cream into butter using a tradition that has been passed down through generations of the family. The cream comes from the farm’s own cows, giving you a closer look at the connection between farming, food and everyday Amish life in Lancaster County. Once the butter is finished, enjoy a taste with crackers and lemonade before taking home a half-pound of freshly churned butter per person. It’s a simple, memorable way for families, couples and curious travelers to experience Amish Country beyond the roadside views.More Things to Do at Old Windmill FarmTake an Amish Farm Tour – Milk a cow, bottle feed calves, gather eggs, meet farm animals and enjoy a hayride around the property.Try the Amish Farm Fun Combo – Add seasonal gardening activities, including planting or harvesting fresh vegetables to take home.Meet & Cuddle Farm Animals – Get up close with goats, piglets, chicks, bunnies, calves and other animals, depending on the season.Book a Seasonal Farm Experience – Fall offerings can include baking bread, churning butter and pressing fresh apple cider in the farmhouse kitchen.Shop Farm-Fresh Goods – Stop by Windmill Harvest for items like raw milk, cheese, meat and canned goods to take home. Learn More about Old Windmill Farm Make a weekend of your visit! Old Windmill Farm is located in the heart of Lancaster County’s Amish countryside, close to restaurants, lodging and other popular attractions in Ronks, Paradise and Strasburg. Where to Eat Near Old Windmill Farm Make your Amish Country visit even more memorable with a meal nearby. Hershey Farm Grand Smorgasbord – Enjoy Pennsylvania Dutch favorites, homestyle dishes, baked goods and a full smorgasbord experience. Dienner’s Country Restaurant – A local favorite for traditional Pennsylvania Dutch comfort food, homemade dishes and buffet selections. Miller’s Smorgasbord – Experience a Lancaster County tradition with a wide selection of Pennsylvania Dutch dishes, carved meats, fresh baked desserts and more. Fireside Tavern – For something a little different, head to nearby Strasburg for steaks, seafood, sandwiches and casual American fare in a cozy tavern setting. More Places to Eat in Lancaster Places to Stay Near Old Windmill Farm Turn your butter-churning experience into an overnight getaway and spend more time exploring Lancaster County’s Amish countryside. Hershey Farm Resort – Relax on a scenic Amish Country property featuring charming guest rooms, countryside views, walking paths, an outdoor pool, and on-site Smorgasbord, gift shop, bakery, and cafe. The Red Caboose Motel at Paradise Station – Spend the night in a restored railroad caboose surrounded by Lancaster County farmland for a stay that’s especially fun for families and train lovers. Fulton Steamboat Inn – A distinctive steamboat-themed hotel with an indoor pool, on-site dining and a convenient location near attractions throughout the Route 30 and Strasburg area. The Cabins at Beaver Creek – Settle into a private cabin surrounded by the peaceful Lancaster County countryside for a quieter, more relaxed Amish Country getaway. More Places to Stay in Lancaster

events.title: Amish Butter Churning at Old Windmill Farm
events.description: Experience a Lancaster County tradition firsthand at Old Windmill Farm, an authentic working Amish farm in Ronks, PA. During this hands-on experience, you’ll learn how to churn fresh cream into butter using a tradition that has been passed down through generations of the family. The cream comes from the farm’s own cows, giving you a closer look at the connection between farming, food and everyday Amish life in Lancaster County. Once the butter is finished, enjoy a taste with crackers and lemonade before taking home a half-pound of freshly churned butter per person. It’s a simple, memorable way for families, couples and curious travelers to experience Amish Country beyond the roadside views.More Things to Do at Old Windmill FarmTake an Amish Farm Tour – Milk a cow, bottle feed calves, gather eggs, meet farm animals and enjoy a hayride around the property.Try the Amish Farm Fun Combo – Add seasonal gardening activities, including planting or harvesting fresh vegetables to take home.Meet & Cuddle Farm Animals – Get up close with goats, piglets, chicks, bunnies, calves and other animals, depending on the season.Book a Seasonal Farm Experience – Fall offerings can include baking bread, churning butter and pressing fresh apple cider in the farmhouse kitchen.Shop Farm-Fresh Goods – Stop by Windmill Harvest for items like raw milk, cheese, meat and canned goods to take home. Learn More about Old Windmill Farm Make a weekend of your visit! Old Windmill Farm is located in the heart of Lancaster County’s Amish countryside, close to restaurants, lodging and other popular attractions in Ronks, Paradise and Strasburg. Where to Eat Near Old Windmill Farm Make your Amish Country visit even more memorable with a meal nearby. Hershey Farm Grand Smorgasbord – Enjoy Pennsylvania Dutch favorites, homestyle dishes, baked goods and a full smorgasbord experience. Dienner’s Country Restaurant – A local favorite for traditional Pennsylvania Dutch comfort food, homemade dishes and buffet selections. Miller’s Smorgasbord – Experience a Lancaster County tradition with a wide selection of Pennsylvania Dutch dishes, carved meats, fresh baked desserts and more. Fireside Tavern – For something a little different, head to nearby Strasburg for steaks, seafood, sandwiches and casual American fare in a cozy tavern setting. More Places to Eat in Lancaster Places to Stay Near Old Windmill Farm Turn your butter-churning experience into an overnight getaway and spend more time exploring Lancaster County’s Amish countryside. Hershey Farm Resort – Relax on a scenic Amish Country property featuring charming guest rooms, countryside views, walking paths, an outdoor pool, and on-site Smorgasbord, gift shop, bakery, and cafe. The Red Caboose Motel at Paradise Station – Spend the night in a restored railroad caboose surrounded by Lancaster County farmland for a stay that’s especially fun for families and train lovers. Fulton Steamboat Inn – A distinctive steamboat-themed hotel with an indoor pool, on-site dining and a convenient location near attractions throughout the Route 30 and Strasburg area. The Cabins at Beaver Creek – Settle into a private cabin surrounded by the peaceful Lancaster County countryside for a quieter, more relaxed Amish Country getaway. More Places to Stay in Lancaster

events.title: Little River Band with Seals & Crofts 2
events.description: The Eagles’ founding member, the late Glenn Frey, knew what he was saying when he dubbed Little River Band “the best singing band in the world.” The current lineup of LRB takes that accolade to heart every time they perform. Through the ‘70s and ‘80s, Little River Band enjoyed huge chart success with multi-platinum albums and chart topping hits like “Reminiscing,” “Cool Change,” “Lonesome Loser,” “The Night Owls,” “Take It Easy On Me,” “Happy Anniversary,” “Lady,” and many more! Experience the timeless harmonies and heartfelt storytelling of Seals & Crofts 2 — a tribute and continuation of the iconic musical legacy of the 1970s soft rock duo, Seals & Crofts. Featuring Brady Seals (cousin of Jim Seals and former member of Little Texas) and Lua Crofts (daughter of Dash Crofts), this dynamic duo brings a fresh and soulful interpretation of the original hits that defined a generation. With voices that echo their legendary family ties and a chemistry that captivates audiences of all ages, Seals & Crofts 2 perform beloved classics like “Summer Breeze,” “Diamond Girl,” and “We May Never Pass This Way (Again),” alongside new original music that honors the spirit and sincerity of the originals. More than just a tribute, Seals & Crofts 2 is a celebration of musical heritage, connection, and the enduring power of melody. Don’t miss this enchanting evening filled with nostalgia, harmony, and artistry that bridges generations.
